newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian may let foreigners buy real estate.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian may let foreigners buy real estate.

text.p: Slovenia's government tabled draft legislation on Thursday that would amend the nation's constitution to enable foreigners to buy real estate in accordance with European Union norms.
"Today the government unanimously determined a proposal for changes to the 68th article of the constitution," government legislative director Lojze Janko told a news conference.

His announcement coincided with a Constitutional Court ruling on Thursday that parliament could not ratify an association agreement with the EU without constitutional changes. As it stands, the constitution prohibits foreigners from owning land in Slovenia.
"Parliament must not ratify the agreement if constitutional changes are not implemented," constitutional judge Peter Jambrek said in his public ruling.
In the association agreement with the EU, signed in June last year, Slovenia agreed to enable foreigners to buy land within four years of the accord taking effect.
Last month the government asked the Constitutional Court to rule on whether ratification could take place prior to any constitutional changes.

"This decision confirms that the 68th article of the constitution prevents Slovenia from advancing towards EU membership. Now it is important that the parliamentary procedure to change the constitution moves fast," Foreign Minister Zoran Thaler said.

European Commission President Jacques Santer said in April that Slovenia's speedy ratification was a pre-condition for the country to be included in the first round of nations to start negotiations on the EU membership, probably in 1998.
